name: a milestone agent dies without returning a bundle — the re-spawn is counted, and not against the node budgets
why: The failure delegation creates. A milestone agent that dies takes a whole milestone's worth of crash window with it: the state file says `node: BRANCH` while commits may or may not exist on a branch nobody has looked at. `milestone agents` is written BEFORE the spawn precisely so this state is legible — it names the branch and the base_sha, which is where re-derivation starts. What this walk asserts is the counter: the re-spawn is charged to attempts['MILESTONE-dispatch:1'], NEVER to TEST:1 or GATE_A:1. A milestone agent that returned no bundle tested nothing and reviewed nothing, and charging it to a node budget hands the milestone a re-run allowance it never spent — verbatim the GATE_A-dispatch lesson, where a checkpointed dispatch spent the findings budget and the gate that actually ran had none left. It also proves the block-open rule: the second milestone agent starts at BRANCH again, because it re-derives from the world rather than resuming mid-itinerary.

steps.observation: The first milestone agent for this milestone never returned a bundle. milestone agents['1'] was open with no history entries after it — the death signature — so before re-spawning I ran git log a1b2c3d..PROJ-1/simulated: no commits, the milestone agent died before it wrote anything. Re-spawned once; the branch already existed and was reused.
